explanation: Overlay loading is a memory management technique used to load only necessary parts of a program into memory at a given time.  This is crucial for running large programs that exceed available memory. Instead of loading the entire program, the loader loads only the initial part (the root segment) and loads additional segments (overlays) as needed, replacing previously loaded segments. This conserves memory by avoiding the need to keep the entire program resident in RAM simultaneously.  The linker plays a key role by defining how these overlays are structured and which segments can replace each other.
syntax: Not directly expressible as a fixed syntax, but rather a linker directive-driven approach. The structure is defined by linker commands specifying segments and their relationships (e.g., which segments can overlay others) within an overlay tree structure.
example_explanation: This example shows a simplified representation of linker commands defining an overlay structure. The `OVERLAY` directive defines an overlay segment.  The `root` segment is the initial part loaded. Segment `A` is part of the root. `segmentD` is an overlay that can replace a portion of memory previously occupied by other segments. The `INCLUDE` directive brings in additional object files (libraries).  During runtime, only the root segment and the currently needed overlay would be in memory, illustrating the space-saving nature of overlay loading.  A real implementation would involve more complex mechanisms for segment management and swapping but this highlights the core concept.
